thread:
Ravi: Noticing a spike in gpu attach failures in ap-south1 since 01:50. Attach latency tail and nvme resets on a few hosts. Can someone take a look?
Nora: Which pool? any node ids?
Ravi: pool=asia-scratch-thinstripe. Example host: gnode-ap-07. dmesg shows repeated nvme controller reset messages: 
```
[01:52:12] nvme0: controller reset due to cmd timeout
[01:52:13] nvme0n1: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
```
Tomas: Ouch. Also seeing SMART reallocated_sector_count bump on gnode-ap-07: `smartctl -A /dev/nvme0n1` reports RAW: 12 -> 45 in last hour.
ops-runner: Correlating with background janitor + scrub runbooks. infra-bot: Alert 1: high nvme-reset-rate in ap-south1 (hosts affected: 5). Correlates with janitor sweep window 01:45-02:00.
Nora: Quick mitigations: 1) pause janitor sweep in ap-south1, 2) lower scrub concurrency, 3) cordon noisy hosts and migrate GPU pods to network-backed-pool. Tomas: I'll run the pause. Command: `infractl jobs pause janitor --region ap-south1`
ops-runner: Paused janitor sweep. infra-bot: Janitor jobs paused in ap-south1 (confirmed).
Ravi: After pause, attach failures dropped but two hosts still show nvme resets. Recommend cordon gnode-ap-07 and gnode-ap-11, drain GPU pods to netpool.
Tomas: Cordon + drain issued: `kubectl cordon gnode-ap-07 && kubectl drain gnode-ap-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Nora: While cordoning, we should schedule vendor firmware. Vendor says firmware 3.0.0 addresses link-level power state transitions that cause resets under intense small-write churn. But it needs node reboot and NVMe secure update.
Ravi: Let's do rolling reboots for the affected AP region during maintenance window Tue 02:00-05:00, after vendor validation. In the meantime, keep janitor paused and run watch.
ops-runner: Also set nr_requests lower on noisy hosts as mitigation: `ssh gnode-ap-07 'echo 64 > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/nr_requests'`
infra-bot: Autoscaler: temporarily divert new attaches to network-backed-pool for ap-south1. New attach requests for canaries will use netpool.
Nora: Cost note: running netpool fallback estimated +$0.03/hr per GPU (egress + persistent-storage premium). Flagging for finance if fallback >12h.
Tomas: Opening vendor ticket (VT-2026) and requesting async traces and recommended firmware.
Ravi: I'll draft the incident note and postmortem skeleton. TL;DR: background janitor+scrub overlap triggered NVMe stress on several drives; vendor firmware needed. Immediate mitigations: pause janitor, cordon noisy hosts, migrate to netpool, schedule firmware roll on maintenance window.
Nora: Thanks all. Keep updates here. :eyes:
